response.headline: Terrain blocking EE and Three signals is the likely cause [terrain_blocking][los_ee][los_three].

causes.explanation: Terrain rises 137 m above the direct line to EE and Three sites 6.5 km away, weakening their signals [los_ee][los_three]; Vodafone's line is clear [los_vodafone], so terrain does not explain poor Vodafone reception.

Only Vodafone has confirmed mast sites within 5 km, while EE and Three sites are 6.5 km away with terrain rising 137 m above the direct line [operators_5km][los_ee][los_three]; crowd-sourced gaps mean other operators cannot be fully excluded [no_site_o2].

Speeds fell 35% over four quarters to 14.4 Mbps while test usage is high at 7.4 devices per 1,000 residents versus a UK median of 3.6 [speed_cell][speed_trend][usage_per_head], suggesting congestion may contribute, though only one quarter of data is available.

The nearest confirmed Vodafone site is 1.4 km north with a clear line of sight [los_vodafone], yet speeds are far below the UK median [speed_cell][speed_1km]; however, an unknown-operator site is only 0.5 km west [nearest_site], so distance alone is unlikely to be the primary cause.
Speeds are low but only one quarter of tests is available and operator coverage at the exact point cannot be confirmed from crowd-sourced site data [speed_cell][operators_5km].

actions.text: Try Vodafone first, as it has the clearest line of sight to a nearby confirmed site [network_comparison][los_vodafone].
Use Wi-Fi calling indoors if your phone and network support it.
Check your address on Ofcom's mobile coverage checker: https://www.ofcom.org.uk/mobile-coverage-checker
Emergency calls work on any available network.

response.best_network: Vodafone is likely best here: clear line of sight to a confirmed site 1.4 km north [network_comparison][los_vodafone]. EE and Three have confirmed sites 6.5 km away but terrain blocks the line of sight [los_ee][los_three]. O2 has no site identified in our data [no_site_o2][network_comparison].
limitations: Sites are approximate; antenna heights assumed; Ofcom figures are area-level.
Causes are inferred from public data, not confirmed: operators' network data is not public.
Ookla speeds are quarterly aggregates with no time-of-day detail; congestion can only be inferred.
No address-level Ofcom coverage; Ofcom figures are for the whole constituency and are predictions.
Mast sites are approximate (crowd-sourced OpenCelliD, OpenStreetMap, Ofcom's licence register) and incomplete, so 'no sites found' is weak evidence.
Line of sight uses a surface model (trees and buildings included) and mostly assumed antenna heights; blocked means a weaker signal, not no signal.
